what: Nutanix sells software that turns ordinary servers into a private cloud. Companies run their applications and data on it in their own data centres or across public clouds, managed through one interface.
customers: Enterprises, government agencies, healthcare and education organisations running their own infrastructure.
money: software subscriptions and support, billed over multi-year terms
moat: Infrastructure software that an organisation's applications and operations are built on, where migration means rebuilding how the data centre runs.
risks: It competes against far larger infrastructure vendors
Growth of about 12% is moderate for a software company
Stock-based compensation is large relative to reported profit
opportunities: Broadcom's changes to VMware licensing have pushed customers to look for alternatives, which has helped it directly
Gross margin of 87% with return on invested capital of 25%
Cash of about $2.4 billion against little debt
watch: Annual contract value growth and new customer additions from VMware displacement.
